problem: The description of the TCP header is wrong. It says TCP has a 20‑byte header plus a 4‑byte option for the checksum, giving 24 bytes total. In reality the TCP checksum is part of the standard 20‑byte header; there is no extra 4‑byte option.
fix: State that TCP uses a 20‑byte header (which already includes the checksum). The total on‑wire size for 500 bytes of data is 20 (header) + 500 (data) = 520 bytes. Then the overhead difference is 520 − 508 = 12 bytes, not 16 bytes.
